content:
Requirement R05 (input): Report Intelligence Data. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to send intelligence data to the command/support chain..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-05.1, F-05.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-05.<F>.1, Be-05.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-05.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Enable the pilot to transmit collected intelligence data to the command/support chain (via aircraft → C2).

**Function candidates:**

**F-05.1 — Compose-and-transmit intelligence report.** The HMI is FOR turning pilot-authored intelligence content (structured fields: observations, classifications, coordinates, free text) into a report that reaches C2. Goal: authoring + dispatch of substantive data.

**F-05.2 — One-action tactical intelligence dispatch.** The HMI is FOR sending a pre-structured/templated intelligence marker (e.g. "target sighted at cursor position") with minimal authoring, prioritizing speed under high workload. Goal: rapid capture-and-send of a known event type.

**F-05.3 — Attach-and-forward captured sensor/context data.** The HMI is FOR bundling already-available data (current sensor snapshot, aircraft position, timestamp) into an outgoing intelligence package. Goal: forwarding machine-held data the pilot flags as intel-relevant, rather than authoring new content.

These are genuinely distinct goals: F-05.1 is authoring-heavy, F-05.2 is speed-optimized minimal input, F-05.3 is packaging existing data with little manual entry.

Which do you want to close on?

Let's go with 1. My idea is to have a panel that you can input these fields via an onscreen keyboard or the physical keyboard, that then gets validated and sent along with metadata such as altitude and the like.

**F-05.1 — Compose-and-transmit intelligence report** (closed).

Note on your description: attaching metadata (altitude, position, timestamp) is F-05.3 territory. For R05 I'll treat the auto-appended metadata as an *envelope* the system adds automatically on send — not a pilot-authored field — so it stays inside F-05.1's authoring goal without pulling in F-05.3's flag-existing-data intent. Flag it if you'd rather metadata be pilot-selectable; that would broaden the function.

Moving to **Behaviour** (fixed modalities: Touch, Keyboard).

**Be-05.1.1 — Touch-only pathway.** Pilot opens the intel report panel on WAD, selects fields by tapping, enters values via an on-screen keypad/keyboard rendered on WAD, taps to cycle categorical fields (classification, event type), then a single validation gate checks completeness/format before a CONFIRM SEND tap. All authoring achievable by touch alone.

**Be-05.1.2 — Keyboard-only pathway.** Pilot navigates fields via bezel OSS (field-step) and enters alphanumeric content via UCP keyboard; categorical fields stepped via bezel rotary; validation gate then CONFIRM via bezel OSS. Fully completable without touching WAD — relevant when gloves/turbulence make touch unreliable.

**Be-05.1.3 — Mixed pathway.** Field selection by Touch, value entry by UCP keyboard (or vice versa), free interleaving; single shared validation gate before send. Adds real value: free-text intel fields are far faster on the physical keyboard while field-picking is faster by touch — the modality-complete redundancy rule requires each work alone, but Mixed is the realistic authoring mode.

Validation gate is shared across all three (single pre-send envelope check), consistent with R01's single-validation-before-CONFIRM pattern.

Which pathway(s) to close on?

**Be-05.1.3 — Mixed pathway** (closed). Note: Be-05.1.1 and Be-05.1.2 remain implicitly satisfied since the modality-complete redundancy rule requires each modality to complete the task alone — Mixed is the primary authoring mode, but the structure must still allow either alone.

Moving to **Structure**. Concrete HMI elements on fixed hardware (WAD touch/keypad, bezel OSS+rotary, UCP keyboard, validation, audio/screen for gate feedback).

**S-05.1.3.1 — Dedicated Intel Report panel (WAD overlay) + UCP keyboard.**
- New WAD overlay layer: form with labeled fields (event type, classification, coordinates, free-text observation).
- Free-text/numeric fields: focus by Touch OR bezel OSS field-step; entry via on-screen keyboard (Touch) OR UCP alphanumeric keyboard — either works per field.
- Categorical fields (event type, classification): Touch-cycle OR bezel rotary step.
- System auto-appends metadata envelope (alt/pos/timestamp) on send — displayed read-only.
- Single validation gate → CONFIRM SEND (Touch OSS on panel + bezel OSS, both live). Gate result via notification strip + audio ping (reuses R02 alert channel).

**S-05.1.3.2 — Intel entry via reused R01-style multi-input panel, extended.**
- Extend the R01 multi-input panel pattern (touch keypad + bezel + keyboard/rotary already proven) with an intel-field mode.
- Same input-redundancy logic as R01/R03; adds report-specific fields and free-text.
- Leaner: reuses existing panel scaffolding and validation-before-CONFIRM rather than a new form. But R01 is numeric-parameter oriented — free-text intel authoring is an awkward fit; risk of overloading that panel.

**S-05.1.3.3 — Map-anchored intel capture + form popup.**
- Pilot marks report location on reused Map view (Touch or TDC cursor), which spawns a compact intel form popup pre-filled with that coordinate; remaining fields entered via on-screen keyboard/UCP.
- Ties authoring to geographic context; strong for coordinate-bearing intel. But drifts toward F-05.3 (packaging existing/contextual data) — keep only if map-anchoring stays optional, not the sole entry path.

**Sharing flag:** the validation gate + CONFIRM/alert channel (notification strip + audio ping) is the same reusable multi-channel alert from R02 — shared, not new. The Intel Report panel itself is R05-specific but could later serve surveillance-data reporting (R for capability 3), which is structurally identical authoring.

Recommendation: **S-05.1.3.1** — cleanest fit for authoring-heavy free-text intel without overloading the numeric R01 panel.

Which to close on?
Let's go with the first one.

**S-05.1.3.1 — Dedicated Intel Report panel (WAD overlay) + UCP keyboard** (closed).

**R05 — Report Intelligence Data — final:**
- **F-05.1** — Compose-and-transmit intelligence report (pilot-authored fields; system auto-appends metadata envelope on send).
- **Be-05.1.3** — Mixed Touch/Keyboard authoring pathway (field selection and value entry freely interleaved; single shared validation gate before send; each modality also complete alone per redundancy rule).
- **S-05.1.3.1** — Dedicated WAD overlay Intel Report form: labeled fields with Touch-OR-bezel focus, on-screen-keyboard-OR-UCP entry, Touch-cycle-OR-rotary categorical fields, read-only auto-metadata, single validation gate → dual-input (Touch/bezel) CONFIRM SEND. Reuses R02 multi-channel alert (notification strip + audio ping) for gate/send feedback.

**Shared elements flagged:** R02 alert channel reused; Intel Report panel is a candidate for reuse in surveillance-data reporting (capability 3, structurally identical authoring) — to be consolidated later.

R05 complete. Ready for the next requirement when you are.
